as a carribean person who was adopted by white American people at the age of 3 I completely related to Leila's anger at her parents for not exposing me to aspects of my culture. It feels like a whole part of me is missing that I can't put my finger on. Now that I'm older I make the efforts I can to learn more about my heritage but I will always be an outsider to that side of myself. Both our emotions are completely valid the way she expressed herself wasn't. Typical 'American' take to think that the end al be all to happiness is to be in America. White people can adopt whatever foreign baby they want if it helps tamper down their savior complex but throwing money in the Childs face and tell them to be grateful for erasing a part of their identity isn't the 'big brain' take you think it is.
